title: Maximum Total Reward Using Operations I
summary: Given an integer array rewardValues, start with a total reward of 0 and no indices marked.
statement: Given an integer array rewardValues, start with a total reward of 0 and no indices marked. You can repeatedly choose an unmarked index i where rewardValues[i] exceeds the current total reward, add rewardValues[i] to the total reward, and mark index i. The goal is to determine the highest possible total reward achievable through optimal operations.
constraints: rewardValues is a nonempty positive-integer array.
Start at total zero; choose each index at most once and only when its reward is strictly greater than the current total.
reference_solution:
def maximum_total_reward(rewardValues):
    reachable=1
    for value in sorted(set(rewardValues)):reachable|=(reachable&((1<<value)-1))<<value
    return reachable.bit_length()-1
known_wrong_solutions:
def maximum_total_reward(rewardValues):
    reachable=1
    for value in sorted(set(rewardValues)):reachable|=(reachable&((1<<(value+1))-1))<<value
    return reachable.bit_length()-1
def maximum_total_reward(rewardValues):
    reachable=1
    for value in sorted(rewardValues,reverse=True):reachable|=(reachable&((1<<value)-1))<<value
    return reachable.bit_length()-1
hints: A bitset can mark every reachable total; reward v may extend only bits at positions below v.
Process distinct rewards ascending and shift the eligible low prefix by v.
reachable |= (reachable & ((1<<v)-1)) << v; answer highest set bit.
Each shift represents exactly one legal append of v, and ascending distinct processing is sufficient because any legal sequence is strictly increasing in chosen reward.
editorial: Each shift represents exactly one legal append of v, and ascending distinct processing is sufficient because any legal sequence is strictly increasing in chosen reward.

tests.explanation: Choose one reward one and then one reward three to total four.
Choosing one, two, four, then six is illegal at the last step; choosing one, four, then six reaches the optimal total eleven.
